summary: Returns the value as a countable number, or throws.
description: A value that can serve as a quantity, a length or a zero-based index: a whole number, not negative, and small enough that integer arithmetic on it is still exact.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a countable number.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not a countable number.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireCountable(0); // => 0
requireCountable(42); // => 42
requireCountable(-1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireCountable(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
